'''Francis Fabien Michel Muguet''' (1955–2009) was a French chemist who advocated open access to information.

==Biography==
Muguet graduated with a Ph.D from [[Texas Tech University]] with a thesis on water chemistry in 1992. His advisor was G. Wilse Robinson.<ref>{{cite book |title= Investigations of Diffuse Intermolecular Electronic Systems |author= Francis F. Muguet, M.S. |date= May 1992 |publisher= Texas Tech University |url= https://ttu-ir.tdl.org/items/77a0e8b4-f8a4-4a82-88ba-99e69f1d97ad |accessdate= July 19, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Muguet |first1=Francis |title=Investigations of diffuse intermolecular electronic systems |date=1992 |publisher=Texas Tech University |url=https://ttu-primo.hosted.exlibrisgroup.com/permalink/f/f2u3nh/01TTU_ALMA21170512180002611 |access-date=19 July 2025}}</ref>
He also held a law degree. He was a researcher at [[ENSTA]] (École nationale supérieure de techniques avancées) from 1993 to 2009 and worked, during the last months of his life, as a consultant for [[International Telecommunication Union]] (ITU) and the [[University of Geneva]].

Defender of the free and open access to scientific content,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.biomedcentral.com/openaccess/archive/?page=features&issue=17 |title=Lobbying for Open Access legislation |access-date=2009-10-18 |archive-date=2009-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091019203121/http://www.biomedcentral.com/openaccess/archive/?page=features&issue=17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> he chaired the Civil Society Scientific Information Working Group, and co-ordinated a group on patents, trademarks and copyrights at the [[World Summit on the Information Society]] (WSIS).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=8194812893544942709 |title=Dr. Francis Muguet's speech at Geneva |access-date=2009-10-18 |archive-date=2011-06-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622092214/http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=8194812893544942709 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=301222277851752196 |title=Dr. Francis Muguet's speech at Tunis |access-date=2009-10-18 |archive-date=2009-04-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090420100508/http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=301222277851752196 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Muguet is also known for designing the pattern of global patronage which aims to answer the legal argument raised against the global license under the Berne Convention on copyright. The sponsorship was supported by his friend [[Richard Stallman]] who co-authored with him the Declaration of Louisiana at a workshop organized by the French Society of the Internet on March 12, 2009. Muguet was then one of the founders of the SARD, a Society of acceptance and distribution of gifts inspired by the principles of global patronage.

Muguet was active in the World Network for Linguistic Diversity and point of contact for the Dynamic Coalition for Linguistic Diversity of the [[Internet Governance Forum]] and a member of [[ICVolunteers]]. From 2001 to 2005, he was Associate Editor MDPI Center Basel.

His daughter found him dead on October 14 after he had not answered his mail for several days.
Following the announcement of his death, a change was made in the process of printing the book ''La bataille Hadopi'', to which he had contributed, dedicating it to him.<ref>{{cite web |title= Francis Muguet est mort |author= Mathieu Pasquini |date= October 17, 2009 |work= In Libro Veritas Bibliotheca |url= http://www.ilv-bibliotheca.net/blog/index.php?post/2009/10/17/Francis-Muguet-est-mort |accessdate= July 10, 2011 |language= fr |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110723155006/http://www.ilv-bibliotheca.net/blog/index.php?post%2F2009%2F10%2F17%2FFrancis-Muguet-est-mort |archive-date= July 23, 2011 |url-status= dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title= La bataille Hadopi |publisher= In libro veritas |year= 2009 |isbn= 978-2-35922-016-2 |language=fr}}</ref>
